manual_review.independent_work: Source download and extraction ran while toolchain installation was active.
findings: The initial installer explicitly used noninteractive mode and completed with a recorded operation status of zero. No input-write or process-kill recovery occurred.
Toolchain installation completed after three blocking polls. One identical output repeat was a root-user warning during redirected installation, not evidence of deadlock.
Configuration first failed because Menhir was absent. The agent installed it and configured successfully.
The first build succeeded but the subsequent functional check could not link the runtime library at the configured installation prefix. Reconfiguration, a second build and installation fixed it.

A diagnostic unsupported compiler option produced an error while the compound shell command returned zero. Install/build commands printed their primary status but still ended with diagnostics; guidance is not runtime enforcement.

findings: Two shell status keyword matches inspect the initial environment; they are not a progress-polling loop.
Mailman option placement, ListManager signature, owner roster, subscription utility, settings attribute and enum types caused diagnosis/recovery work.
At tool ordinals 11 and 13, a Python exception was followed by successful diagnostics, leaving shell exit 0. General exit-status guidance did not prevent every masked main-command error.
No process waiting occurred in either current Mailman or the preceding waiting-candidate trajectory; improvements cannot be attributed solely to process guidance.
The final supplied iterative check succeeded; all three native verifier tests ran and passed.

limitations: Two single candidate observations with historical references, not a concurrent randomized comparison or full local-24 evaluation.
General waiting guidance and first-party catalog deduplication changed jointly; this is not an ablation separating their effects.
Evaluator revisions, dependency routing, calendar time and resource competition differ across batches; historical original raw trajectories remain unavailable.
Both current tasks have no observed OOM. Historical baseline CompCert and original candidates have OOM observations; sampled memory peaks do not prove OOM.
Mailman has no process calls in either the previous waiting run or this run, so its changes cannot be attributed solely to process polling.
Total tokens fall versus baseline, but combined uncached input is nearly unchanged. Token ratios are not monetary savings.
Mailman retains one partial interrupted service-command process stream; archive CRC and file hashes pass and all 24 provider requests reconcile, but not every process stream is complete.
Prompt guidance did not eliminate all wrong API guesses, semantically repeated build work or masked main-command failures. No runtime enforcement was added.
